subtitle: A Disputed Prince in the Courts of War and Verse

panels.shot: epic three-quarter view, low-angle wide of a young prince seated between palm-leaf manuscripts and a sword, Shravanabelagola hills faint in the distance
panels.action: Durvinita sits on a carved wooden throne, one hand resting on a sheathed sword, the other over open palm-leaf manuscripts, eyes steady as distant hills and fort walls loom behind him.

dialogue.text: In Gangavadi’s fifth-century dust, Prince Durvinita fights for a throne—but later ages remember his hands not only on the sword, but on the great poets’ words.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं सदी की गंगवाड़ी की धूल में, राजकुमार दुर्विनीत गद्दी के लिए लड़ता है—पर आने वाली सदियाँ उसे तलवार के साथ-साथ कवियों के शब्दों के लिए भी याद रखती हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in from a bird’s-eye view over Gangavadi, settling on the prince beside a window overlooking fields and forests
panels.action: A teenage Durvinita, in simple royal cloth and minimal ornaments, leans in a palace window that opens onto terraced fields and thick forests, a palm-leaf book balanced on his knee.

dialogue.text: In the land later called Gangavadi, the Western Ganga line holds a frontier between Tamil plains and Deccan plateaus. Inscription and memory fix one king’s name: Durvinita.

i18n.hi: जो धरती बाद में गंगवाड़ी कहलाएगी, वहाँ पश्चिमी गंगा वंश तमिल मैदानों और दक्कन पठार के बीच की सरहद थामे है। शिलालेख और स्मृति एक नाम पर ठहरते हैं: दुर्विनीत।

panels.shot: interior medium shot, dim audience hall, elders in debate leaving Durvinita half-lit at the edge
panels.action: Durvinita stands at the edge of a council hall where ministers and generals argue around his father’s empty throne, his face tense as he hears talk of rival claimants.

dialogue.text: The stone records are terse, but they speak of a struggle: a disputed succession, factions at court, and a prince whose right to rule is challenged.

i18n.hi: पत्थर के लेख थोड़े हैं, पर संघर्ष की कहानी कहते हैं: विवादित उत्तराधिकार, दरबार की गुटबाज़ी, और एक राजकुमार जिसकी राजसत्ता पर ही सवाल है।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of a frontier encampment, banners snapping, Durvinita conferring with commanders
panels.action: Durvinita, now armored, stands beside war tents and elephants, conferring with commanders as dust swirls and distant hills mark the line of Pallava territory.

dialogue.text: Durvinita’s power will not rise in peace. On one side, Pallava opposition presses from Kanchi; on another, rivals question his crown. His reign begins amid steel and suspicion.

i18n.hi: दुर्विनीत की ताकत शांति से नहीं उठती। एक ओर कांची से पल्लव दबाव, दूसरी ओर ताज पर सवाल उठाते हुए प्रतिद्वंदी। उसका राज लोहे और अविश्वास के बीच शुरू होता है।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of Durvinita on horseback facing an unseen army across a valley
panels.action: Durvinita sits firm on a horse at a ridge, a small escort behind him, staring across a valley where enemy standards line the horizon under a hot, hazy sky.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions praise victories and alliances, not fear. They hint that against Pallava power, Durvinita stands his ground, and seeks backing from stronger Deccan neighbours.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख डर नहीं, जीत और दोस्ती का ढोल पीटते हैं। इशारा इतना कि पल्लव शक्ति के सामने दुर्विनीत डटा रहता है, और ताकतवर दक्कनी पड़ोसियों से सहारा खोजता है।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a tent, Durvinita alone by lamplight with manuscripts beside weapons
panels.action: Inside a quiet war tent, a lamp glows over a low table where palm-leaf manuscripts lie next to a laid-down sword; Durvinita bends over the leaves, lips moving silently as he reads.

dialogue.text: But tradition remembers another battlefield: the page. Later writers say that even in such years, Durvinita’s nights were with grammar, story and verse.

i18n.hi: पर परंपरा एक और रणभूमि याद रखती है: पन्ना। कहा जाता है इन हिंसक बरसों में भी दुर्विनीत की रातें व्याकरण, कथा और कविता के साथ कटती थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot in a court library, shelves of palm-leaf bundles, Durvinita listening to a Jain scholar
panels.action: In a cool pillared chamber lined with palm-leaf bundles, Durvinita sits cross-legged, attentive, as a Jain monk-like scholar gestures toward a manuscript in front of them.

dialogue.text: The age around him is changing. Sanskrit courts link Deccan kings; Prakrit and early Kannada stir. Jain teachers move between them, carrying logics, grammars and tales.

i18n.hi: उसके चारों ओर युग बदल रहा है। संस्कृत दरबार दक्कन के राजाओं को जोड़ते हैं; प्राकृत और आरंभिक कन्नड़ जाग रहे हैं। जैन आचार्य इन सबके बीच चलते हैं, तर्क, व्याकरण और कथाएँ लिए।

panels.shot: slow push-in close shot on Durvinita’s face as he traces letters on a palm leaf
panels.action: Durvinita’s fingers gently trace incised letters on a palm leaf, his brows furrowed in concentration, a faint smile forming as he follows the script’s curves.

dialogue.text: Durvinita’s inscriptions do not boast of authorship. Yet later memory, in works like Kavirajamarga, speaks of a Ganga king who loved words as much as war.

i18n.hi: दुर्विनीत के शिलालेख लेखन का घमंड नहीं करते। पर कविराजमार्ग जैसी बाद की कृतियाँ एक ऐसे गंगा राजा का ज़िक्र करती हैं जिसे शब्द उतने ही प्यारे थे जितना युद्ध।

panels.shot: wide shot of court sabha, poets and scholars from different traditions presenting before Durvinita
panels.action: Durvinita sits on a modest but elevated throne in a sabha hall while Brahmin and Jain scholars, each in their own dress, stand in a semi-circle, holding manuscripts as if presenting.

dialogue.text: Here, at a Ganga court on a southern frontier, scholars of different paths gather. The record’s silences leave details unclear, but the pattern is plain: this throne is open to many learnings.

i18n.hi: देक्‍खन की इस दक्षिणी सरहद पर गंगा दरबार में भिन्न मार्गों के पंडित जुटते हैं। अभिलेख चुप हैं, पर तस्वीर साफ है: यह राजसिंहासन कई तरह की विद्या के लिए खुला है।

panels.shot: medium shot, Durvinita listening as a poet recites, subtle focus on the poet’s expressive gesture
panels.action: A poet in fine but simple cloth recites with one hand raised, eyes closed; Durvinita leans forward, elbow on knee, fully absorbed, the hall quiet around them.

dialogue.text: Later tradition even claims Durvinita touched Bharavi’s Kiratarjuniya—with commentary or patronage—and turned the Brihatkatha into Sanskrit. These are stories of reputation, not signed works.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा तो यह भी कहती है कि दुर्विनीत ने भारवि के किरातार्जुनीय पर हाथ रखा—व्याख्या से या सरंक्षण से—और बृहत्कथा को संस्कृत में ढाला। यह हस्ताक्षरित नहीं, यश की कथाएँ हैं।

panels.shot: side-on medium shot of Durvinita and a Jain grammarian debating over a manuscript
panels.action: Durvinita and a Jain scholar sit facing each other across a low desk, a grammar text laid between them, both pointing at the same line, mid-discussion.

dialogue.text: Names like the Jain grammarian Pujyapada appear in the tradition around him. Whether they sat in this very hall we cannot prove, but Ganga kings did work with such Jain minds.

i18n.hi: जैन व्याकरणाचार्य पूज्यपाद जैसे नाम उसके आसपास की परंपरा में दिखते हैं। यही सभा साझा की या नहीं, कहना मुश्किल है, पर गंगा राजा ऐसे जैन मनीषियों के साथ काम ज़रूर करते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of palace terrace, Durvinita looking toward Shravanabelagola hills where a basadi stands
panels.action: From a palace terrace, Durvinita looks out over a landscape dotted with small shrines; in the distance, low rocky hills like those of Shravanabelagola rise, bearing a Jain basadi silhouette.

dialogue.text: The same Western Ganga line will later mark Shravanabelagola with Jain basadis and colossal stone forms. Durvinita’s reign stands in that early chain of Jain patron kings.

i18n.hi: यही पश्चिमी गंगा वंश आगे चलकर श्रवणबेलेगोला को जैन बसदियों और विराट पत्थर प्रतिमाओं से चिन्हित करेगा। दुर्विनीत का शासन उन शुरुआती जैन-पालक राजाओं की कड़ी में खड़ा है।

panels.shot: documentary-style close-up on an inscription being carved, Durvinita watching from the side
panels.action: A stonecutter chisels neat lines into a rock face as priests and scribes look on; Durvinita stands aside, arms folded, watching as the words of his reign take form.

dialogue.text: Nallala and Gummareddipura inscriptions, carved in his time, speak of alliances and victories, of a king recognized by powerful neighbours beyond Gangavadi.

i18n.hi: नल्लला और गुम्मरेड्डिपुरा के शिलालेख, जो उसके समय में उकेरे गए, जीतों और संधियों की बात करते हैं, एक ऐसे राजा की जो गंगवाड़ी से परे शक्तिशाली पड़ोसियों द्वारा मान्यता पाता है।

panels.shot: interior shot, Durvinita with ministers reviewing maps and a manuscript side by side
panels.action: Durvinita sits with his ministers before a spread of painted maps and a neatly bundled manuscript, one hand on the border lines, the other resting lightly on the manuscript.

dialogue.text: Steel wins recognition. Yet the court’s language—Sanskrit for diplomacy, Prakrit and early Kannada for local ties—is also a tool. Durvinita’s house learns to speak across regions.

i18n.hi: लोहे से मान मिलता है। पर दरबार की ज़बान—संधि के लिए संस्कृत, और लोगों के लिए प्राकृत व आरंभिक कन्नड़—भी हथियार है। दुर्विनीत का घर सीखता है कि अलग-अलग प्रदेशों की भाषा में कैसे बोले।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot suggestion, older Durvinita in the same hall, more manuscripts piled high
panels.action: An older Durvinita, hair slightly greying, sits in the same sabha hall now crowded with stacked palm-leaf bundles and visiting scholars, the atmosphere one of settled, busy learning.

dialogue.text: By the time later authors look back, they see his reign not only as a hard-won rule, but as a moment when a frontier court steps fully into the wider Sanskrit and Jain intellectual world.

i18n.hi: जब बाद के लेखक पीछे मुड़कर देखते हैं, तो उन्हें उसका राज सिर्फ मुश्किल से जीती गद्दी नहीं दिखता, बल्कि वह घड़ी दिखती है जब एक सरहदी दरबार पूरी तरह व्यापक संस्कृत और जैन बौद्धिक संसार में पाँव रखता है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Durvinita’s eyes as they move from a sword rack to a manuscript stack
panels.action: Durvinita’s gaze shifts from a rack of neatly hung swords to a high stack of manuscripts on a shelf, his expression calm, reflective, as if weighing them silently.

dialogue.text: The historian’s caution remains: we cannot sign verses in his hand. But we can see the pattern of patronage and study that made such stories about him possible.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार की सावधानी फिर भी रहती है: हम उसके हाथ के लिखे श्लोक पर हस्ताक्षर नहीं कर सकते। पर हम वह सरंक्षण और अध्ययन का ढाँचा देख सकते हैं जिसने उसके नाम पर ऐसी कथाएँ जन्म दीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a modern scholar reading an inscription, Durvinita faintly superimposed like memory
panels.action: In a modern archive-like setting, a scholar leans over a rubbing of a Ganga inscription; above and behind, faintly like a memory, Durvinita sits in his old court among books and advisors.

dialogue.text: From stone and later texts, one image emerges: a prince who fought for a throne, and a king whose court bound itself to the poets, grammarians and Jain teachers of his age.

i18n.hi: पत्थर और बाद की पुस्तकों से एक छवि उभरती है: एक राजकुमार जो गद्दी के लिए लड़ा, और एक राजा जिसका दरबार अपने को कवियों, व्याकरणाचार्यों और जैन आचार्यों से जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: final contemplative medium shot, Durvinita on palace steps at dusk with a palm leaf in hand
panels.action: At dusk, Durvinita sits on the palace steps, the court behind him fading into shadow, holding a single palm leaf up to the remaining light, face calm and thoughtful.

dialogue.text: Durvinita’s story reminds us that a king’s quiet choices—to read, to listen, to host many tongues—can shape a kingdom’s place in history as deeply as any spear or siege.

i18n.hi: दुर्विनीत की कहानी बताती है कि राजा के शांत फैसले—पढ़ना, सुनना, और कई ज़बानों को जगह देना—भी किसी भाले या घेराबंदी जितना ही गहरे में उसके राज्य की जगह इतिहास में तय कर सकते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: A Disputed Prince in the Courts of War and Verse
subtitle_i18n.hi: युद्ध और कविता की अदालतों में झगड़ालू राजकुमार
